root.name: Sicilian Defense: Classical Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 Nc6

overview: Black develops the queenside knight before choosing a structure, which allows 6.Bg5 (Richter-Rauzer), 6.Bc4 (Sozin), 6.Be3 (English-Attack-style) or 6.Be2. The strong-player branch is 6.Bg5 e6 7.Qd2 Be7 8.O-O-O O-O with opposite-side castling: White attacks on the kingside with f4 and Black counters with ...a6 and ...b5 or ...Nxd4 and ...Qa5. The play is theoretical and tactical.

white_ideas.idea: Richter-Rauzer: Bg5, Qd2, O-O-O and kingside pawn storm
Sozin: Bc4 pointing at f7 and Be3, Qe2 for a quick attack
Meet ...a6 and ...b5 with f4, Nxc6 and central breaks

black_ideas.idea: Trade the d4 knight with ...Nxd4 and use the c-file
...e5 or ...d5 breaks to open the centre in several lines

typical_structures.structure: Open Sicilian with half-open c-file and d6 pawn, often with opposite-side castling

character.notes: Both sides castle opposite wings in the main lines and the tactics are forcing; one mistake can lose quickly.

gambit.notes: No sacrifices as a rule; pawns traded evenly.

soundness.notes: Sound; main line at the top level.

structure.notes: Every Sicilian is semi-open with a half-open c-file.

level.notes: Richter-Rauzer and Sozin lines are long and need to be known; I rate it Advanced with modest confidence.
